question_text: Find the general term $u_n$ of the geometric sequence which has:

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up equations $u_1 r^4 = 324$ and $u_1 r^9 = 78732$

subparts.solution:
$$u_5 = u_1 r^4 = 324 \quad \dots (1)$$
$$\text{and } u_{10} = u_1 r^9 = 78\,732 \quad \dots (2)$$
$$\text{Now } \frac{u_1 r^9}{u_1 r^4} = \frac{78\,732}{324} \quad \{(2) \div (1)\}$$
$$\therefore r^5 = 243$$
$$\therefore r = \sqrt[5]{243}$$
$$\therefore r = 3$$
$$\text{Using (1), } u_1(3)^4 = 324$$
$$\therefore 81u_1 = 324$$
$$\therefore u_1 = 4$$
$$\text{Thus } u_n = 4 \times 3^{n-1}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: For a geometric sequence, the $n$th term is $u_n = u_1 r^{n-1}$. Dividing higher-order terms by lower-order terms eliminates $u_1$.
step_by_step: Express $u_5$ and $u_{10}$ in terms of $u_1$ and $r$: $u_1 r^4 = 324$ and $u_1 r^9 = 78732$.
Divide the second equation by the first: $r^5 = 243$.
Substitute $r = 3$ back into equation (1) to find $u_1 = 4$.
Substitute $u_1$ and $r$ into the general formula $u_n = u_1 r^{n-1}$.

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up $u_1 r^7 = -10$ and $u_1 r^{11} = -160$ and dividing

subparts.solution:
$$u_8 = u_1 r^7 = -10 \quad \dots (1)$$
$$\text{and } u_{12} = u_1 r^{11} = -160 \quad \dots (2)$$
$$\text{Now } \frac{u_1 r^{11}}{u_1 r^7} = \frac{-160}{-10} \quad \{(2) \div (1)\}$$
$$\therefore r^4 = 16$$
$$\therefore r = \pm \sqrt[4]{16}$$
$$\therefore r = \pm 2$$
$$\text{If } r = 2, \text{ then using (1), } u_1(2)^7 = -10$$
$$\therefore 128u_1 = -10$$
$$\therefore u_1 = -\frac{10}{128} = -\frac{5}{64}$$
$$\text{Thus } u_n = -\frac{5}{64} \times 2^{n-1}$$
$$\text{If } r = -2, \text{ then using (1), } u_1(-2)^7 = -10$$
$$\therefore -128u_1 = -10$$
$$\therefore u_1 = \frac{10}{128} = \frac{5}{64}$$
$$\text{Thus } u_n = \frac{5}{64} \times (-2)^{n-1}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: An even power equation $r^4 = k$ yields both positive and negative roots ($r = \pm \sqrt[4]{k}$), each yielding a valid sequence.
step_by_step: Divide equation (2) by equation (1) to get $r^4 = 16$.
Solve for $r$ giving two solutions: $r = 2$ or $r = -2$.
State the two corresponding general term formulas.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting the negative root when taking an even root ($r = \pm 2$).
